Registered 2026-10-21, before any answer under the corrected control and lint was seen. A setting passes only if it meets all four:
1. Gate: at least 2 of 3 suites pass the validity gate.
2. Catches finding 9: in each gate-passing suite, at least one AC-018 test fails at b5d42890 and passes on the control.
3. Catches finding 10: in each gate-passing suite, at least one test under AC-013, AC-014, AC-015 or AC-024 fails at bc57eb74 and passes on the control.
4. Precision: no test fails on the control in a gate-passing suite. Each control failure is read by hand against the control's code; one that exposes a real control defect corrects the control and is re-scored, never discounted.

reply.summary:
I wrote 49 Playwright acceptance tests in four files under acceptance/web-calculator/, and every acceptance criterion has at least one. I ran the whole suite with --repeat-each 2 twice. Against a temporary mock that follows the plan, all 98 runs passed. Against the blank index.html, all 98 runs failed, every one on an assertion or on a locator action that found no element; that run took about 140 s. With the mock's hover styles removed, the AC-022 tests failed, which confirms they detect a missing hover state. I deleted the temporary index.html afterwards, so only the test files remain.

Files:
- calculator-clicks.spec.mjs covers AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011, AC-012 and AC-023. AC-002 is one test that reloads the page for each digit 0–9.
- calculator-keyboard.spec.mjs covers AC-013 to AC-017 and AC-024. Each runs three times: with focus on the document body, on a calculator button, and on the theme control. The button differs per criterion (1, =, +, ., C, backspace), so a focused button that would also react to Enter is covered.
- theme.spec.mjs covers AC-018, AC-019 and AC-020, each with the theme control activated three ways: click, Enter and Space. AC-019 and AC-020 close the page and open a new one in the same browser context. One extra AC-018 test checks both criteria at once: Enter on the focused theme control must switch the theme and also do equals (2 + 3 gives 5, as in AC-014).
- layout-and-states.spec.mjs covers AC-021 at 320×568, and AC-022 for every calculator button and the theme control in both themes, for mouse hover and for focus reached with the Tab key.

Things the implementer should know:
- The combined Enter test conflicts with the plan as written. The plan calls preventDefault on Enter in its keyboard handler, which stops Enter from also activating the focused theme control. The implementation must make Enter on that control both switch the theme and do equals.
- Elements are found by role and name, using the plan's choices: the display as role "status"; buttons by their exact labels; the backspace button by a name matching backspace, delete or ⌫; the theme control by a name matching theme, dark, light or mode.
- AC-021 and AC-022 have no single Playwright matcher, so a helper adds a read-only property to the element that does the check live on the page, and the test asserts it with toHaveJSProperty, which retries. Running style transitions are finished before the starting styles are recorded.
- The runner uses Chromium only and opens the page from a file:// address, so AC-001 is checked in Chromium and not in Firefox.

tests.title: AC-001 Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL in a current Chromium-based or Firefox browser, with no server process running, displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.

AC-002 For each digit d from 0 through 9, after a fresh page load, clicking the button labelled 1 and then the button labelled d results in the display area showing the value formed by the digit 1 followed by d.
AC-003 The page shows operator buttons labelled +, -, × and ÷, a decimal point button labelled ., an equals button labelled =, a clear button labelled C, and a backspace/delete button.
AC-004 After a fresh page load, clicking the buttons 1, 2 in sequence results in the display area showing the value 12.
AC-005 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.
AC-006 After a fresh page load, clicking 7, -, 1, 0, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value -3.
AC-007 After a fresh page load, clicking 6, ×, 7, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 42.
AC-008 After a fresh page load, clicking 8, ÷, 2, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 4.
AC-009 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, ., 5, +, 2, ., 2, 5, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 3.75.

AC-011 After a fresh page load, clicking 5, +, 3 and then C results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load, and then clicking 2, +, 2, = results in the display area showing the value 4.
AC-012 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, 3 and then the backspace/delete button results in the display area showing the value 12 and its text not containing 123.
AC-023 Loading index.html shows the calculator without any login, sign-up or credential prompt, and every criterion above passes without the user entering any credential.
AC-013 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27. — focus on the document body

reply.summary:
I wrote 56 Playwright tests in four files under acceptance/web-calculator/, covering every criterion from AC-001 to AC-024. Each test title starts with the criterion's ID and words; tests for variants add a suffix in brackets.

- clicks.spec.mjs: AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011, AC-012 and AC-023. It has one test per digit for AC-002, and AC-001 checks that the page opened from a file:// URL. AC-011 and AC-012 check clear and backspace. AC-023 checks there are no login, sign-up or password elements and that a calculation works.
- keyboard.spec.mjs: AC-013 to AC-017 and AC-024. Each runs with focus on the document body and on several kinds of button: digit, operator, decimal point, equals, clear, backspace and the theme control. This includes Enter pressed on a focused digit button, which must not also click the button.
- theme.spec.mjs: AC-018 to AC-020. The theme control is activated by click, Enter and Space, the theme is switched several times, and the body background colour must differ between light and dark. One combined test presses Enter on the focused theme control and checks that equals is done (AC-013) and the theme changes (AC-018). The persistence tests close the page and reopen it in the same browser context.
- layout.spec.mjs: AC-021 checks at a 320×568 viewport that the page is no wider than 320 pixels and that every button, the display and the theme control fit fully inside it. AC-022 checks hover and Tab-key focus for every button and the theme control, in both light and dark themes.

The tests find buttons by role and accessible name. They use the plan's ids `#display` and `#theme-toggle` for the display and the theme control.

Results: with the system's command (repeated twice) against the blank index.html, all 56 tests failed on an assertion or on a locator that finds no element, never on navigation or a script error. Against a quick reference calculator I wrote outside the checkout (in /tmp), all tests passed. I deleted the temporary blank index.html; only the four test files remain.

One test goes beyond the plan: the plan cancels Enter's default action on every focused button. But the spec counts Enter as a way to activate the theme control, so the AC-018 and AC-019/AC-020 tests that press Enter on the focused theme control require the theme to toggle. An implementation that follows the plan literally will fail them.

reply.summary:
I wrote 122 Playwright acceptance tests in six files under acceptance/web-calculator/. Every acceptance criterion has at least one test.

**Files and what they cover:**
- **clicks.spec.mjs** (AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011, AC-012): clicking the buttons for each sum, all ten digits for AC-002, the button set, clear (C) returning the display to its exact first text, and backspace.
- **keyboard.spec.mjs** (AC-013 to AC-017, AC-024): each criterion is tested with focus in 8 places — the document body, a digit, an operator, the decimal point, equals, C, backspace and the theme control. Focus is moved there without a click or key press, so the page load still counts as fresh.
- **theme.spec.mjs** (AC-018 to AC-020): the theme control is activated by click, Enter and Space. The tests check that the attribute switches between light and dark, that the body background differs between themes, and that dark and light survive closing and reopening the page. One extra test covers Enter pressed while the theme control has focus: it must both run equals (display shows 27, per AC-013) and switch the theme.
- **layout.spec.mjs** (AC-021): at 320×568, the page's scroll width is at most 320 and every button, the display and the theme control lie within 0–320 px.
- **states.spec.mjs** (AC-022): each of the 19 buttons, in both themes, must look different when hovered and when focused with the Tab key. Running colour transitions are skipped to their end before styles are read.
- **access.spec.mjs** (AC-023): no password field, dialog or login/sign-up wording, no browser pop-up, and a calculation works.

**How elements are found:** by role and visible name — the display as `status`, buttons by their labels, and backspace by a name containing backspace, delete or ⌫. The theme control has no name set in the plan, so it is found by the plan's id `#theme-toggle`.

**Results:**
- **Blank index.html:** I ran the required command one file at a time with `--repeat-each 2`. All 244 runs failed, each on an assertion or on a click that found no element; none failed on navigation or a script error. I then deleted the blank index.html.
- **Throwaway implementation:** I also ran all 122 tests once against a quick implementation I put in /tmp, outside the checkout, using my own config. All 122 passed, so the tests can be met.

**Things the implementer should know:**
- **AC-001 runs in Chromium only.** The runner has no Firefox installed, so the Firefox half of that criterion is not checked.
- **Enter on the theme control:** the plan cancels Enter's default action so a focused calculator button isn't pressed twice. Done that way, Enter would never switch the theme. The tests require Enter on the focused theme control to do both: run equals and switch the theme.

tests.title: AC-023 Loading index.html shows the calculator without any login, sign-up or credential prompt, and every criterion above passes without the user entering any credential.

AC-001 Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL in a current Chromium-based or Firefox browser, with no server process running, displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.
